subject: How to rotate collapsed node names in circular view?

messages.author: b3ebe0a3130f4831
messages.subject: How to rotate collapsed node names in circular view?
parts:
Hello!

I have two related questions around generating a tree figure using ggtree.

1) I'm working with a large phylogeny in ggtree, and have collapsed and renamed over 100 clades to allow focus on the clades I am interested in. 

My basic code is:

p1 = ggtree(tree, layout = 'circular') + geom_tiplab2(color="black")
p2 = collapse(p1, 5406) + geom_cladelabel(node=5406, "Archaea")
p3 = collapse(p2, 5161) + geom_cladelabel(node=5161, "Chloroflexi")
p4 = collapse(p3, 5154) + geom_cladelabel(node=5154, "Bacteroidetes")
p5 = collapse(p4, 5119) + geom_cladelabel(node=5119, "Firmicutes")

jpeg(filename = 'filename.jpeg', width = 1500, height = 4000, quality = 100)
p5
dev.off()

If I export p5 tree as a svg or jpeg, the node names I have added are not rotated with their branches - they are all oriented as normal text. The tip labels of the uncollapsed clades are rotated with the angle of the branches. How do I rotate the new node names? Or how do I apply a name to a collapsed clade such that it is treated as a new tip and new tip label, which would then rotate like the other tips (i.e., am I doing this wrong)?

2) Also, how do I rename internal nodes with a name of my choice, and then how do I export the tree file (not image, the tree as text in nexus or newick) with the node label changed? So for p2 clade in example above, how do I include the node name "Archaea" in an exported tree? I've been working with treeio and ape, and I can't find this option with either package.

Thanks in advance for any clarity on this!

best,
Laura

messages.author: cec41188340e8212
messages.subject: Re: How to rotate collapsed node names in circular view?
parts:
You can use tidytree package (also my pkg) for easy manipulation of tree object.


> tr <- read.tree(text = "((a,(b,c)),d);")
> require(tidytree)
> dtr = as_data_frame(tr)
> dtr$label[dtr$node ==5] = "X"
> dtr$label[dtr$node ==6] = "Y"
> as.phylo(dtr)

Phylogenetic tree with 4 tips and 3 internal nodes.

Tip labels:
[1] "a" "b" "c" "d"
Node labels:
[1] "X" "Y" NA

Rooted; no branch lengths.
> as.phylo(dtr) %>% write.tree
[1] "(d,(a,(b,c)NA)Y)X;"
​

messages.subject: Re: How to rotate collapsed node names in circular view?
parts:
Hi Guangchuang,

Here is an example of the node names not rotating like the tip labels:

library(package = 'ggtree')

tr <- read.tree(text = "((a,((b,c),(d,e))),f);")

p1 = ggtree(tr, layout = 'circular') + geom_tiplab2(color="black")
p2 = collapse(p1, 11) + geom_cladelabel(node=11, "Clade DE")
p3 = collapse(p2, 10) + geom_cladelabel(node=10, "Clade BC")



See the attached .png files for what the trees look like:
p1: all tip labels rotated with their branches, nothing collapsed
p2: one collapsed clade, tree orients that one so label is at 90 degrees, all ok
p3: two collapsed clades - clades are not not rotated with branches. (I need clade BC to aim downwards, not be oriented as normal written text)

Any insight you could offer would be much appreciated. Thank you for the note on tidytree, that solved an immediate problem and let me use iTOL to output a labeled collapsed tree.

best,
Laura

messages.author: cec41188340e8212
messages.subject: Re: How to rotate collapsed node names in circular view?
parts:
I added a new parameter clade_name in collapse, so that you can set the label of corresponding clade when collapsing.

Then using geom_nodelab to display the labels, which works similar to geom_tiplab.

library(package = 'ggtree')

tr <- read.tree(text = "((a,((b,c),(d,e))),f);")

p1 = ggtree(tr, layout = 'circular') + geom_tiplab2(color="black"

)
p2 = collapse(p1, 11, "Clade DE")
p3 = collapse(p2, 10, "Clade BC")

p3 + geom_nodelab(aes(subset = node == 10 | node == 11, angle=angle), hjust=-.1)

You need to install github version of ggplot2 and ggtree (v >= 1.13.0.005) to have this new feature of setting clade_name.



​
